powerGrafana.subtitle: Build a Grafana panel JSON envelope against the curated catalog, then copy it into your own dashboard.

workflow.title: How it works
workflow.step1: Draft with Helix or write / paste a Grafana panel JSON envelope in the editor.
workflow.step2: Click copy to clipboard to grab the JSON.
workflow.step3: In Grafana, choose add panel â†’ edit JSON and paste it in.
workflow.note: The browser never pushes panels to Grafana directly â€” you stay in control of what lands on your dashboards.

powerGrafana.intro: Build a Grafana panel JSON envelope against the curated panel-builder catalog below. The browser does not push the panel to Grafana; copy your JSON into your existing Grafana dashboard editor.

panelTypes.title: Curated panel types
panelTypes.intro: These are the panel types the curated catalog exposes. The Helix natural-language drafter refuses any panel type outside this list.

datasourceTypes.title: Curated datasource types
datasourceTypes.intro: These are the datasource types the curated catalog exposes, with their canonical UIDs. The Helix natural-language drafter refuses any datasource type outside this list.

tables.title: Curated table catalog (postgres targets)
tables.intro: These tables are the only tables the curated catalog exposes for postgres-target rawSql. The Helix natural-language drafter refuses any postgres query referencing tables outside this list.

aiDrafter.title: Helix natural-language Grafana panel drafter
aiDrafter.description: Describe the panel you want in plain English (e.g. "show me a daily time series of how far I drove this month"). Helix proposes a typed Grafana panel JSON draft you can apply to the editor with one click; it never pushes the panel to Grafana directly.
aiDrafter.promptPlaceholder: e.g. show me a daily time series of how far I drove this month
aiDrafter.applyTooltip: Copy the proposed panel JSON into the editor above. You can still edit it before clicking Copy to clipboard.
